groups.title: Hotwire Architecture Concepts
groups.question: You want your Rails app to feel like a single-page app, with tabs that switch without reloads and comments that appear live for everyone, without writing a React frontend. Explain how Turbo does this.

followUps.Turbo Drive for fast page navigation: What does Turbo Drive change about clicking a link?
followUps.Turbo Frames for partial page updates: How does a Turbo Frame update just part of the page?
followUps.Turbo Streams for server-pushed DOM upda: How do Turbo Streams update several places on the page?

evidence.text: Turbo Drive intercepts link clicks and form submissions.
It fetches the new page and swaps the body instead of doing a full reload.
This keeps scripts and styles loaded, so navigation feels faster.

notEnough: Only saying Turbo makes pages faster.

evidence.text: A Turbo Frame wraps a section of the page with an id.
Links and forms inside it replace only that frame with the matching frame from the response.
This gives tabs, inline edits and pagination without custom JavaScript.

notEnough: Only saying frames update parts of a page.

evidence.text: Turbo Streams send actions like append, replace or remove for specific targets.
They can arrive in an HTTP response or be broadcast over WebSockets.
One response can update several parts of the page at once.

notEnough: Only saying streams update the DOM.

groups.title: Stimulus and Progressive Enhancement
groups.question: You need a dropdown that opens on click and a chat where new messages appear for everyone instantly. Explain how Stimulus and Action Cable help.

followUps.Stimulus controllers and data attributes: How does Stimulus connect JavaScript to HTML?
followUps.Real-time features with Action Cable Web: How do Action Cable and Turbo Streams deliver live updates?

evidence.text: Controllers are attached to elements with data-controller attributes.
Data attributes also wire up actions and target elements.
It adds behaviour on top of server-rendered HTML rather than replacing it.

notEnough: Only saying Stimulus is a JS framework.

evidence.text: Action Cable adds WebSocket channels to Rails.
Clients subscribe to a channel for the data they are viewing.
Turbo Stream messages broadcast over it update every connected client.

notEnough: Only saying Action Cable uses WebSockets.

groups.title: Hotwire Setup and Tooling
groups.question: You are adding Hotwire to an existing Rails app and creating your first Stimulus controller. Explain the setup.

followUps.Installing Hotwire with turbo-rails gem: What does the turbo-rails gem provide?
followUps.stimulus-rails gem and controller genera: How do you add and generate Stimulus controllers?

evidence.text: It adds the Turbo JavaScript library to the app.
It provides view helpers for frames and streams.
It adds model helpers for broadcasting updates.
stimulus-rails adds Stimulus to the import map or bundler setup.
A generator creates new controller files.
Controllers live in app/javascript/controllers and are loaded automatically.

notEnough: Only saying you install the gem.

groups.title: Interactive UI Patterns
groups.question: You want users to edit a recipe title in place, and everyone viewing the recipe list should see new recipes appear. Explain how you would build both.

followUps.Inline editing with Turbo Frames workflo: How would you build inline editing with a Turbo Frame?
followUps.Broadcasting live updates from Active Re: How does a model broadcast changes to everyone viewing the list?

evidence.text: Wrap the title display in a Turbo Frame.
The edit link loads a form into the same frame.
Saving returns the updated display in that frame, so only that area changes.

notEnough: Only saying you use a frame.

evidence.text: Models can broadcast Turbo Streams when records are created, updated or destroyed.
The page subscribes to the stream for that list.
Every viewer's page updates without polling.
